title: CSR portal fixes: disclosure checkbox, policy search, missing[] panel
acceptance: Disclosure questions render as a required checkbox (labelled, aria-required) and the submitted answer is boolean true, never a string
Policy lookup uses GET /api/v1/policies?q=<text> and renders items from {items, matchedOn} (with matched field shown); no exact-lookup call remains in search.js
Required-items panel lists IntakeStep.missing[] entries and updates after each answer
The CSR todo test in tests/ui/csr.test.mjs is a real passing test and the page.route workaround is removed
node --test --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning tests/ui/csr.test.mjs tests/unit/web/csr/ passes with Chromium actually run
Unit tests in tests/unit/web/csr/ cover disclosure coercion, search response mapping and missing[] rendering
brief: You must run the CSR flow in Chromium via the Playwright test (Playwright at /opt/node-tools/node_modules, browsers /opt/pw-browsers) before declaring done. Blocker S2-EXP-03-4 is in org/hubs/experience.jsonl. (1) src/web/csr/assisted.js/app.js: question type disclosure currently renders as a text fx-field and sends a string; server rejects with 422 (fraud_disclosure on personal_auto). Render a required checkbox ('I confirm the caller was read the disclosure') and send boolean true; unchecked blocks submit with an inline accessible error. Add a pure helper for answer coercion so it is unit-testable in tests/unit/web/csr/assisted.test.mjs or a new test file in that folder. (2) search.js: replace exact policy lookup with GET /api/v1/policies?q= (URL-encode q), response {items, matchedOn}; show each item with policy number, insured name, and which field matched. Handle empty results and errors via errors.js. Check architecture/core-runtime-api.md and docs/api-reference.md for the item shape. (3) Show IntakeStep.missing[] (array of missing required field/question ids) in the required-items panel; use friendly labels where known and keep it aria-live polite. Strings go in strings.js. (4) tests/ui/csr.test.mjs: it contains a page.route workaround that rewrites the disclosure answer to boolean; remove it and flip the t.todo test (the one titled 'CSR can answer the fraud disclosure through the UI alone') to a real passing test. Do not touch src/web/claimant, shared, package.json. Report Chromium test output in your result.

verdicts.reason: All criteria met; 31 tests pass with Chromium run, no skips; checkbox boolean true, GET /policies?q, missing[] panel, workaround removed
